speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any recent injury or trauma to that specific finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That mechanism sounds very concerning for a fracture or significant ligament injury. Did you hear a distinct "pop" or "snap" at the moment of impact?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray right hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the right hand shows no bone fractures or dislocations visible; soft tissue swelling is noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray rules out a fracture, pointing toward a soft tissue injury like a ligament sprain or tendonitis. Given the specific mechanism of the finger being pulled, did you experience a sudden loss of grip or the feeling that your finger was "stuck" or dislocated during the pull?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the resting position of extension strongly suggest an injury to the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. Did you notice any visible gap or step-off in the tendon on the palm side of the finger near the distal joint?

REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound right ring finger flexor tendons.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound of the right ring finger flexor tendons shows a complete discontinuity of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at the distal interphalangeal joint with a visible retracted tendon stump and absence of continuity to the distal phalanx. Surrounding soft tissue edema is present. No calcifications or masses are identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Complete rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon of the right ring finger.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
